messages.subject: formula interpretation - space and time
parts:
Hi all,

I have a question about the interpretation of a particular formula. I am setting up the following model for bru():

form <- count ~ Intercept(1) + 
  car_space_deviation(polygon_idx, model="besag", graph=g1, constr=T) +
  rw1_year_effect(year_idx, model="rw1",  constr=T,
             group=polygon_idx, control.group=list(model="besag", graph=g1, constr=T))

The way I understand this formulation, there is (term 1) a global intercept, (term 2) a CAR structured deviation from the global intercept per spatial polygon, and (3) a first-order random walk per polygon, where the random walk in a given polygon is influenced by 1st order neighbors according to a CAR structure. Is that interpretation correct?

If so, how is the info shared for the rw1? Is the value for t+1 for a focal polygon based on a mean that comes from the values at t from the focal polygon plus its neighbors? 

Thanks for any clarification.

Best,
Tim

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] formula interpretation - space and time
parts:
Hi Tim,

the "group" feature defines a latent field with Kronecker product
precision/covariance structure. The interpretation in your case is
that the difference between the values at one timepoint and the next
is given by a spatial besag model, i.e. the random walk increments are
spatially correlated:
x_{t+1}(s) = x_t(s) + v_t(s)
where the increments v_t(s) are spatially correlated besag fields,
independent for each time point.

Your last guess isn't quite right, as that would involve a
non-kronecker precision structure.
